check.title: Check a document: the article, the quote, the date.
check.lead: NormaAI looks in the document for the references to an article, a recital or an annex, with the act they belong to, and compares them with the official text in three ways.

1.title: The article exists
1.body: The article and every paragraph cited must be in the text in force, that is the latest consolidated version. If the article was in an earlier version, the report says it was repealed or renumbered.

2.title: The quote is word for word
2.body: The words in quotation marks are looked for in the article cited. Every number and every short word, such as "not" or "or", must match: "48 hours" where the law says "72 hours" is a quote to correct. Only punctuation, accents, a word split at a line break and one wrong letter in a long word are tolerated. If the words are in another article, or only in an earlier version, the report says so.

3.title: The provision has not changed since the date of the document
3.body: If you give the date of the document, NormaAI compares the provision in force on that day with today's. If it has changed, you see the text then and the text now, with the differences.

result.title: What you get
result.body: A report that sorts the references by what there is to do: to correct, to check, fine. For each one you find the line of the document, the outcome, the official text and the link to the text on EUR-Lex or Normattiva.

limits.title: What it does not do
limits.body: It does not say whether the reference is the right one for your case, or whether an exact quote leaves out an exception: it checks the wording, the assessment stays yours. References are found automatically and one written in an unusual way can be missed. It is not legal advice.

watch.title: A warning when a provision you cite changes.
watch.body: After the check NormaAI keeps the list of the provisions the document rests on: act, article, version and a fingerprint of the text. At every new version of the official text it compares them again and tells you which documents to review, because a provision they cite has changed or is no longer there.

csrd.inReason: You exceed both cumulative thresholds: net turnover above 450 million euro and more than 1,000 employees on average (Directive 2013/34/EU, Art. 19a(1)). The management report must include the sustainability information.
csrd.inNote1: In Italy, Legislative Decree 125/2024 applies from the financial years starting from {date} to the large undertakings that were not already reporting (Art. 17(1)(b)).
csrd.borderHeadline: Outside the CSRD obligation today, but on the edge of the threshold.
csrd.borderEmployees: You exceed the employee threshold but not the turnover one: since the rule is cumulative, you are outside the obligation today, but a rise in turnover or a change of perimeter is enough to bring you in.
csrd.borderTurnover: You exceed the turnover threshold but not the employee one: since the rule is cumulative, you are outside the obligation today, but net hiring or a consolidation can bring you in.
csrd.borderListed: You are a listed company below the thresholds: Art. 19a looks at size, not at listing, but the position of a listed company has to be confirmed case by case (regulated-market obligations, group perimeter).
csrd.borderMargin: You are outside the obligation today, but close to a threshold: small changes in headcount, turnover or consolidation perimeter make you swing in and out from one financial year to the next.
csrd.borderCheck: This is the case where a precise check on the accounts is worth the most.

aiAct.notAnswered: Answer the four AI questions to assess the transparency obligations of Art. 50.
aiAct.noneHeadline: From your answers, the transparency obligations of Art. 50 do not concern you directly.
aiAct.noneReason: None of the four situations of Art. 50 applies. Outside Art. 50 does not mean outside the AI Act.
aiAct.noneNote1: AI literacy (Art. 4, applicable from {date}): anyone who provides or uses AI systems takes measures to support the AI literacy of their staff, without having to guarantee a specific level.
aiAct.noneNote2: Prohibited practices (Art. 5): applicable from {date}, for example inferring people’s emotions in the workplace; from {added} the prohibitions of points (ba) and (bb) of paragraph 1 are added.
aiAct.noneNote3: General-purpose AI models: for those who provide them the obligations of Chapter V apply from {date}.
aiAct.noneNote4: High-risk systems: the rules apply from {annexIII} for the systems of Annex III and from {annexI} for those of Annex I (Art. 113).
aiAct.inHeadline: Art. 50, applicable from {date}, covers the situations you indicated.
aiAct.inReason1: Mind who the addressee is: some obligations fall on whoever provides the system, others on whoever uses it. If your role is only that of deployer, the provider obligations fall on your provider, and vice versa.
aiAct.inReason2: The information must be given in a clear and distinguishable manner, at the latest at the time of the first interaction or exposure (Art. 50(5)).
aiAct.inNote1: Penalties: up to 15 million euro or, for an undertaking, up to 3% of total worldwide annual turnover, whichever is higher; for SMEs, start-ups included, the lower of the two applies (Art. 99(4) and (6)).
aiAct.inNote2: In Italy, Law 132/2025 designates AgID and ACN as National Authorities for artificial intelligence (Art. 20(1)).
aiAct.inNote3: The rules on the high-risk systems of Annex III apply from {date} (Art. 113).

chat.title: Chatbots and assistants: the person must know they are talking to an AI
chat.requirement: AI systems meant to interact directly with people must be designed and developed so that the person is informed they are interacting with an AI, unless this is obvious to a reasonably informed and attentive person.
chat.exception: Exception: systems authorised by law to detect, prevent, investigate or prosecute criminal offences. If you buy the chatbot from a third party, the design obligation is the provider’s, but checking that it complies is in your interest.

gen.title: Generated content: machine-readable marking
gen.requirement: Providers of systems that generate synthetic content (audio, images, video or text) must ensure the outputs are marked in a machine-readable format and detectable as artificially generated or manipulated.
gen.exception: Exceptions: standard editing assistance functions or functions that do not substantially alter the input data. For systems placed on the market before {applies} the deadline to comply is {legacy} (Art. 111(4)).

emo.title: Emotion recognition and biometric categorisation: inform the people exposed
emo.requirement: Whoever uses an emotion recognition or biometric categorisation system informs the natural persons exposed to it about how the system operates.
emo.exception: Mind the prohibitions applicable from {prohibitions}: inferring emotions in the workplace and in education institutions is prohibited, except for medical or safety reasons (Art. 5(1)(f)).

deep.title: Deepfakes and published AI texts: disclose their origin
deep.requirement: Whoever uses a system that generates or manipulates image, audio or video content constituting a deepfake must disclose that the content has been artificially generated or manipulated. The same applies to AI-generated texts published to inform the public on matters of public interest.
deep.exception: Exceptions: for evidently artistic, creative or satirical works it is enough to disclose the existence of the generated content without hampering the work; for texts, the obligation does not apply where there is human review or editorial control and a natural or legal person holds editorial responsibility.

work.notAnswered: Answer the questions on AI in the employment relationship to assess this section.
work.noneHeadline: From your answers, the rules on AI in the employment relationship do not concern you today.
work.noneReason: None of the situations listed concerns the company.
work.noneNote: If you introduce AI tools that affect decisions, the organisation of work or safety, run the check again: Legislative Decree 179/2026 (Articles 41 and 42) and Art. 4 of the AI Act apply.
work.inHeadline: The rules on AI in the employment relationship cover the situations you indicated.
work.inHeadlineProhibited: One of the situations you indicated is a practice prohibited by the AI Act; the others carry obligations.
work.inFromLabel: Legislative Decree 179/2026, Articles 41 and 42, in force from {date}

reasons.dec: An AI system contributes to decisions on the employment relationship: Art. 41 of Legislative Decree 179/2026 applies.
reasons.org: An AI system affects organisation, pace, how work is carried out or safety: Art. 42 of Legislative Decree 179/2026 applies.
reasons.uso: Staff use AI tools: Art. 4 of the AI Act and Art. 42(3) of Legislative Decree 179/2026 apply.
reasons.prof: Intellectual profession using AI: Art. 13 of Law 132/2025 applies.
reasons.emo: Inferring the emotions of workers is among the practices prohibited by Art. 5 of the AI Act.

work.inNote1: Art. 41 does not treat the search for and selection of applications as final decisions on the establishment of the relationship; AI systems for recruitment or selection are in any case listed in Annex III, point 4, of the AI Act.
work.inNote2: Law 132/2025 refers to the same information duties: the employer informs the worker of the use of AI in the cases and in the manner of Art. 1-bis of Legislative Decree 152/1997 (Art. 11(2)).

emotions.title: Inferring the emotions of workers: a prohibited practice
emotions.requirement: The use of AI systems to infer the emotions of a person in the workplace is prohibited, except where the system is intended to be used for medical or safety reasons.
emotions.exception: Prohibition applicable from {date} (Art. 113, third paragraph, point (a)).

decisions.title: Decisions on the employment relationship: never automatic only
decisions.requirement: Final decisions on the establishment, modification or termination of the relationship, including disciplinary measures and performance evaluations, may not be taken solely on the basis of automated processing: the final decision is reserved to a natural person with effective and autonomous power.
decisions.exception: The worker’s consent is not an exception. Dismissals and decisions in breach are null and void (Art. 41(4)). The search for and selection of applications are not final decisions on the establishment of the relationship.

information.title: Information before starting and reasons on request
information.requirement: Before the processing starts the employer fulfils the information duties of Art. 1-bis of Legislative Decree 152/1997. The worker may obtain, on request and through a natural person, intelligible reasons for the decision that concerns them.
information.exception: Art. 1-bis covers fully automated decision-making or monitoring systems; the information must also be given to the trade union representatives (Art. 1-bis(1) and (6)).

highRisk.title: High-risk systems in the workplace: inform workers and their representatives
highRisk.requirement: AI systems for recruitment or selection and those for decisions on the terms, promotion or termination of the relationship are listed in Annex III, point 4, of the AI Act. Before putting them into service or using them in the workplace, the employer informs the workers’ representatives and the workers concerned.
highRisk.exception: Obligation of the deployers of high-risk systems: it applies from {date} (Art. 113).

riskAssessment.title: Risk assessment: AI goes into the document
riskAssessment.requirement: The use of AI systems that affect the organisation of work, production pace, how work is carried out or decision-making relevant to safety is assessed within the risk assessment of Art. 28 of Legislative Decree 81/2008.

training.title: Information and training of workers on the risks of AI
training.requirement: Employers ensure adequate information and training of workers on the specific risks connected with the use of AI systems and on the prevention and protection measures adopted.

literacy.title: AI literacy of staff
literacy.requirement: Whoever uses AI systems takes measures to support the AI literacy of their staff.
literacy.exception: The obligation does not require guaranteeing a specific level of literacy. Applicable from {date} (Art. 113).

clients.title: Intellectual professions: inform the client
clients.requirement: The information on the AI systems used by the professional is communicated to the recipient of the service in clear, simple and exhaustive language.
clients.exception: AI is allowed only for instrumental and support activities, with the intellectual work that is the object of the service prevailing (Art. 13(1)).

register.title: Registration on the ACN platform

register.exception: ACN communicates the entry in the list of essential or important entities (Art. 7(3)); from 15 April to 31 May of each year those who received the communication provide or update the further information (Art. 7(4)).

governance.title: Management and governing bodies: approve and oversee
governance.requirement: They approve how the cybersecurity risk-management measures are implemented, oversee the implementation of the obligations and are responsible for infringements.

measures.title: Cybersecurity risk-management measures
measures.requirement: Adopt appropriate and proportionate technical, operational and organisational measures; supply chain security is among the minimum elements (Art. 24(2)(d)).
measures.exception: Deadlines: for the entities entered in the list in 2026 the baseline security measures are due by {measures2026} (ACN Determination No 127434/2026, Art. 1(1)); for those entered in 2025 the deadline is eighteen months from receiving the communication of entry (ACN Determination No 379907 of 19 December 2025, Art. 3(1)).

incidents.title: Notification of significant incidents to CSIRT Italia
incidents.requirement: Early notification within 24 hours of becoming aware of the significant incident, notification within 72 hours, final report within one month of the notification.
incidents.exception: Deadlines: for the entities entered in the list in 2026 the obligation runs from {incidents2026} (ACN Determination No 127434/2026, Art. 1(2)) and the CSIRT contact person must be designated by 31 December of the year of entry (ACN Determination No 314287/2026, Art. 7(1)); for those entered in 2025 the deadline is nine months from receiving the communication of entry (ACN Determination No 379907 of 19 December 2025, Art. 3(2)).

activities.title: List of activities and services
activities.requirement: From 1 May to 30 June of each year, starting from the first communication of entry in the list, the entities communicate and update on the platform the list of their activities and services, with the relevance category of each.

reasons.fab: Manufacturer: it manufactures the products, or has them manufactured and markets them under its own name or trademark, or puts them into service for its own use (Art. 3, point (18)).
reasons.imp: Importer: it places on the Union market a product from a third country (Art. 3, point (20)).
reasons.dis: Distributor: it makes the product available on the market without being its manufacturer or importer (Art. 3, point (21)).
reasons.mod: Modification of machinery already placed on the market or put into service: if substantial, it brings the obligations of the manufacturer (Art. 18).

machinery.inNote1: The Regulation covers machinery, interchangeable equipment, safety components, lifting accessories, chains, ropes and webbing, removable mechanical transmission devices and partly completed machinery (Art. 2(1)).
machinery.inNote2: Products placed on the market in conformity with Directive 2006/42/EC before {date} may continue to be made available on the market (Art. 52(1)).

conformity.title: Essential requirements, technical documentation, conformity assessment, CE marking
conformity.requirement: Design and manufacture in accordance with the essential health and safety requirements of Annex III; draw up the technical documentation (Annex IV, Part A), carry out the conformity assessment procedure of Art. 25, draw up the EU declaration of conformity and affix the CE marking (Art. 10(1) and (2)).
conformity.exception: The technical documentation and the EU declaration of conformity stay at the disposal of the authorities for at least 10 years (Art. 10(3)). The instructions for use accompany the machinery and may be provided in digital format (Art. 10(7)).

partlyCompleted.title: Partly completed machinery: technical documentation and declaration of incorporation
partlyCompleted.requirement: For partly completed machinery the manufacturer draws up the technical documentation of Annex IV, Part B, and the EU declaration of incorporation.

importer.title: Import only compliant products and check the manufacturer’s work
importer.requirement: Place on the market only compliant machinery or related products; before placing them, ensure that the manufacturer has carried out the conformity assessment procedure (Art. 13(1) and (2)).
importer.exception: A copy of the EU declaration of conformity stays at the disposal of the authorities for at least 10 years (Art. 13(8)).

distributor.title: Before selling: CE marking, declaration of conformity, instructions
distributor.requirement: Before making the product available on the market, verify that it bears the CE marking and is accompanied by the EU declaration of conformity and by the instructions for use.
distributor.exception: Distributors act with due care in relation to the requirements of the Regulation (Art. 15(1)).

ownBrand.title: Under your own name or trademark you become the manufacturer
ownBrand.requirement: An importer or distributor that places a product on the market under its own name or trademark, or modifies a product already placed on the market in a way that may affect compliance, is considered a manufacturer and takes on the manufacturer’s obligations.

modification.title: Substantial modification: whoever makes it takes on the manufacturer’s obligations
modification.requirement: Whoever carries out a substantial modification of machinery or of a related product is considered a manufacturer and is subject to the related obligations.
modification.exception: A modification is substantial when, by physical or digital means and not foreseen by the manufacturer, it creates a new hazard or increases an existing risk and requires new guards or protective devices with a change to the safety control system, or additional measures for stability or mechanical strength (Art. 3, point (16)).

data.title: 2. Data processed
data.intro1: In the application, for registered users:

app.1: Account: email, name, password (stored only as a bcrypt hash), role, organisation, active status, creation date.
app.3: Clients, that is the companies analysed: name, sector, number of employees, turnover, jurisdictions, applicable regulations.
app.4: Conversations: questions and answers with their metadata (for example the sources cited), linked to the user and, where indicated, to the client.
app.5: Documents uploaded for the answers: the file is processed and deleted; what remains is the extracted text, in chunks indexed with the organisation identifier.
app.6: Checked documents: the file you upload to have its legal references checked is processed in memory and is not stored. What remains is the file name, its SHA-256 fingerprint, the dates, the references found (for each: at most 160 characters of context, the quotes and the outcome) and the provisions of law the document depends on.
app.7: Assessments (gap analyses) and alerts generated for each client.
app.8: Event log: action, outcome, user, organisation, IP address, date and time.
app.9: The company profile filled in the forms is kept in the browser (sessionStorage) and sent to the API together with the question.

site.1: Request for the Codex, for a demo or for the analysis after a free check: email, organisation name, role and originating form (for the checkers also the outcome and, for the AI Act, the situations ticked). The request is received by a serverless function on Vercel: the data is written to the function logs and, when email sending is configured, emailed to info@normaai.org through Resend. It is not saved in an application database.
site.2: Email: the data contained in the messages sent to info@normaai.org.
site.3: Visit statistics: Vercel Web Analytics, without cookies and without identifying the visitor.

basis.title: 3. Legal basis and purposes

items.1: Providing the service and managing the account: performance of a contract (Art. 6(1)(b) GDPR).
items.2: Security of the service (event log, blocking of repeated sign-in attempts, rate limits, spam control): legitimate interest (Art. 6(1)(f) GDPR).
items.3: Sending the Codex and following up on the same subject with whoever requested it: legitimate interest (Art. 6(1)(f) GDPR). You can object at any time by replying to the email received or by writing to info@normaai.org.
items.4: Replying to those who write to us: legitimate interest or pre-contractual measures.

basis.p: The data is neither sold nor used for advertising profiling. It is shared only with the providers listed in section 4, to deliver the service.

processors.title: 4. Sub-processors and providers

items.1: Hetzner Online GmbH (Germany): the server planned for the API, the database and the search index. That is where the application keeps its data; the question and the retrieved passages go instead to the language-model provider (item 3).
items.2: Vercel Inc. (USA): hosting of the site and the interface, with the server-side functions in the Frankfurt region, including the function that receives the Codex and free-checker requests. Visit statistics without cookies.
items.3: Google LLC (Gemini API, USA): the language model that generates the answers. It receives the question, the company profile if entered and the retrieved passages of law. It is the default provider today: the choice is a configuration setting, and the code also supports Anthropic and OpenRouter.
items.4: Resend, Inc. (USA): sending of transactional emails (Codex delivery, notification of new requests).
items.5: Cloudflare, Inc. (USA): DNS of the normaai.org domain and routing of incoming mail: messages written to info@normaai.org pass through Cloudflare’s mail servers before reaching the destination mailbox. Site traffic does not go through Cloudflare’s proxy.

processors.p: For providers based in the United States, transfers rely on the standard contractual clauses included in their data processing agreements.

items.1: Application data: for the whole duration of the relationship. There is no automatic deletion on expiry. The organisation’s administrator can export the data and delete clients, conversations, assessments, alerts and indexed chunks from the application at any time; every user can delete their own conversations. To close the accounts and the organisation write to info@normaai.org.
items.2: Backups: the backup script copies the database every night and keeps the copies for 30 days on the server. Deleted data may remain in a backup for up to 30 days.
items.3: Codex and free-checker requests: they stay in the info@normaai.org mailbox until you ask for deletion, and in the serverless function logs for Vercel’s retention period. The Codex is a public file: its address does not expire.
items.4: Event log: in the server logs, with their rotation.
items.5: Data in the browser: see the <cookie>cookie policy</cookie>.

p.1: You can request access, rectification, erasure, restriction, portability and object to processing by writing to <mail>info@normaai.org</mail>. You can also lodge a complaint with the Italian data protection authority (Garante per la protezione dei dati personali).
p.2: In the application, without writing to us: the administrator can export all the organisation’s data in JSON and erase its contents; every user can delete their own conversations.
p.3: If your data was entered by an organisation that uses NormaAI (for example as an analysed client company), the request goes to that organisation, which is the controller; if it reaches us, we forward it.

p.1: NormaAI uses a generative language model from an external provider (today, by default, Google Gemini) to write the answers from the passages retrieved from the corpus: official texts of EU acts published on EUR-Lex (CSRD, CSDDD, AI Act, DORA, NIS2, EU Taxonomy, GDPR, CRA). All outputs are generated by an artificial intelligence system, may contain errors and need to be checked by a professional. The notice appears in the application, on the Ask page and in the reports.
p.2: NormaAI makes no automated decisions with legal effects on people: it produces analyses that a professional evaluates.

thirdParty.title: 4. Third-party tools
thirdParty.p1: The site loads Vercel Web Analytics, which uses neither cookies nor local storage and collects aggregate visit statistics without identifying the visitor. There are no other third-party scripts: no Google Analytics, Tag Manager, advertising pixels or social plugins. The fonts are served from our own domain.
thirdParty.p2: If tools using cookies or identifiers were introduced in the future, this page would be updated and consent would be asked before activation.

basis.title: 5. Legal basis and consent
basis.p: Strictly technical storage, such as the language cookie, is exempt from prior consent under Art. 122 of the Italian Privacy Code (Legislative Decree 196/2003) and the guidelines of the Italian data protection authority (Decision No 231/2021). That is why NormaAI shows no accept-or-reject banner: it shows a notice with a link to this page and the "Got it" button.

manage.title: 6. How to manage the storage
manage.p: You can delete the data from the browser settings (site data). Signing out deletes the tokens and the demo flag. If you block local storage, access to the reserved area does not work, because the session tokens are kept there; without the language cookie the site goes back to Italian.

contacts.title: 7. Contact
contacts.p: For any request about data processing write to <mail>info@normaai.org</mail>. See also the <privacy>Privacy Policy</privacy>.

security.title: Security
security.intro: The security measures present in the NormaAI code and those still missing. The code is public: every section names the files it is taken from, so whoever has to assess us can check instead of trust.

hosting.title: 1. Where the site, the API and the data run
hosting.p1: The public site and the application interface are hosted on Vercel; the server-side functions run in the fra1 region (Frankfurt). The API and the databases (PostgreSQL for the data, Qdrant for the search index, Redis for cache and sessions) are designed to run on a Hetzner server in Germany.
hosting.p2: In the production configuration the only service exposed to the internet is Caddy, which terminates TLS with Let’s Encrypt certificates (ports 80 and 443) and forwards requests to the application on an internal network. The application has no public ports, runs in a container without root privileges, with a read-only filesystem and no additional Linux capabilities.

model.title: 2. The language model
model.p1: The answers are written by a language model from an external provider, chosen in the configuration (setting llm_provider). Today the default value is gemini: Google Gemini, from a US company. To generate an answer, the question, the company profile if entered and the passages of law retrieved from the corpus are sent to the model provider, which processes them on its own systems.
model.p2: The provider can be changed in the configuration: the code also supports Anthropic and OpenRouter. Today there is no mode in which the answers are generated entirely on our servers.

access.title: 3. Access and sessions

items.1: You sign in with email and password. Passwords are stored only as bcrypt hashes with an individual salt.
items.2: The password check takes the same time even when the email does not exist, so neither response times nor error codes reveal which accounts exist.
items.3: After 5 failed attempts, access for that email is blocked for 5 minutes.
items.4: Sessions use JWT tokens signed with RS256: a private key signs, a public key verifies. In production the application refuses to start without RSA keys. The access token lasts 60 minutes, the refresh token 7 days.
items.5: Every renewal invalidates the previous token. If a token already used is presented again, the whole token family is revoked and the user has to sign in again. Signing out revokes the tokens in use.
items.6: The list of revoked tokens is in Redis. In production, if Redis does not respond, tokens are rejected rather than accepted.
items.7: Three roles: admin, member, viewer. API calls are rate-limited per user or, if anonymous, per IP address.
items.8: In the browser the tokens are kept in localStorage and deleted at sign-out (see the <cookie>cookie policy</cookie>).

access.p: There is no two-factor authentication and no SSO: see section 11.

isolation.title: 4. Separation between organisations
isolation.p: Each organisation sees only its own data. For the tables holding the organisations’ data the separation is enforced by the database, not only by the application.

items.1: PostgreSQL applies Row Level Security policies to the tables holding the organisations’ data (clients, conversations, assessments, alerts and invitations): every row is visible only in the session of the organisation it belongs to. The users and organisations tables have no such policies, by design: sign-in, token renewal and registration look the user up before an organisation context exists. For these two tables the separation is enforced by the application’s queries.
items.2: The application connects with a dedicated non-superuser role (normaai_app), because PostgreSQL ignores the policies for superusers and table owners. In production, if the connected role is a superuser, the application refuses to start.
items.3: The organisation context is set on every transaction and cleared when the connection goes back to the pool: it cannot leak from one request to the next.
items.4: The answer cache uses keys that include the organisation: an answer computed for one client is never served to another.
items.5: In the search engine every chunk of an uploaded document carries the organisation identifier. A search returns the organisation’s chunks plus the shared regulatory corpus; a search without an organisation returns only the shared corpus, never other people’s documents.
items.6: A test with two organisations runs in CI on PostgreSQL with a non-superuser role and fails the build if one organisation sees the other’s data.

documents.title: 5. Uploaded documents
documents.p1: An uploaded document (PDF, HTML or image, up to 50 MB) is written to a temporary file, processed and deleted at the end of processing, even if it fails. What remains is the extracted text, split into chunks and indexed in the search engine with the organisation identifier.
documents.p2: The organisation’s administrator can export all the organisation’s data in JSON and delete clients, conversations, assessments, alerts and indexed chunks in bulk. Deletion requires explicit confirmation and is recorded in the event log.
documents.p3: A document uploaded to have its legal references checked takes a different path: the file is processed in memory and is not stored. What remains is the file name, its SHA-256 fingerprint, the dates, the references found (for each: at most 160 characters of context, the quotes and the outcome) and the provisions of law the document depends on.

headers.title: 6. HTTP headers, CORS and IP addresses

items.1: The site sends Content-Security-Policy, X-Content-Type-Options, X-Frame-Options (DENY), Referrer-Policy, Permissions-Policy and Strict-Transport-Security. The API sends the same headers (HSTS in production) and does not expose the server name.
items.2: CORS accepts only the origins listed in the configuration. In production a wildcard origin prevents start-up.
items.3: The client IP address, used for rate limits and for the event log, is read from the position added by our proxy and not from the first value of X-Forwarded-For, which anyone can forge.

links.title: 7. Codex download
links.p: The Codex is a public PDF file of the site: whoever requests it through the form receives its address, which is neither signed nor expiring. Requests go through a serverless function on the same domain, with a honeypot field that silently discards forms filled in by automated programs. The API also contains a route with HMAC-SHA256 signed links valid for 30 days, but the site does not use it today.

audit.title: 8. Event log
audit.p1: Successful and failed sign-ins, sign-outs, token renewals and reuses, creation and deletion of clients and conversations, questions, document uploads, exports and erasures are recorded as structured events with user, organisation, IP address, date and time and outcome.
audit.p2: Today these events end up in the application logs on the server. There is no separate long-term archive yet and no export ready for auditors: retention is that of the server logs.

backup.title: 9. Backups
backup.p1: The repository contains the backup script, meant to be started by cron every night at 02:00: it runs pg_dump of the PostgreSQL database in compressed format, checks that the archive is readable with pg_restore --list and keeps the copies for 30 days in the backups/ folder of the same server.
backup.p2: The script neither encrypts the file nor copies it to another system: the weekly copy to external storage is a documented manual procedure, not an automatic one. Qdrant and Redis are not backed up: the index is rebuilt with a new indexing, the cache is ephemeral by design. The restore procedure is documented in the repository.

items.1: The code is public on <github>GitHub</github> under the MIT licence.
items.2: On every push and pull request the CI runs ruff (lint and format), mypy (blocking on the authentication, database and audit modules), the backend tests on real PostgreSQL, Qdrant and Redis, type-check, tests and build of the frontend, the Docker image build with a Trivy scan, Gitleaks on the whole git history, Bandit and the generation of a CycloneDX SBOM.
items.3: CodeQL analyses Python and JavaScript/TypeScript with the security-extended queries on every push to the main branch and every week.
items.4: No release has been published yet. The release workflow starts from a version tag: it builds the image, blocks it if Trivy finds critical or high vulnerabilities for which a fix exists, and attaches the SBOM to the release. Dependabot proposes dependency updates.
items.5: .env files and .pem keys are excluded from the repository; the CI fails if it finds API keys or private keys in tracked files.

items.1: No SSO (SAML or OpenID Connect) and no two-factor authentication: you sign in with email and password only.
items.2: No SOC 2 or ISO 27001 certification and no formal third-party penetration test. The automatic scans in CI do not replace it.
items.3: No encryption at rest managed by the application: data protection on disk is that of the server.
items.4: No long-term archive of the event log and no automatic backup copy outside the server.
items.5: The prompt injection filter records the attempts but does not block the input. The real defence is structural: the user’s text never enters the system prompt and the citations are checked against the retrieved passages.

report.title: 12. Reporting a vulnerability
report.p1: Write to info@normaai.org with the subject [SECURITY] NormaAI, explaining how to reproduce the problem and its impact. Do not open a public issue on GitHub.

items.3: Fix or mitigation of critical and high reports within 30 days.
items.4: No monetary reward; credit in the release notes, if welcome.

report.p2: Security fixes go to the main branch. No release has been published yet.
report.p3: For security questionnaires or for the template data processing agreement (Art. 28 GDPR, in the docs/legal/ folder of the repository) write to the same address.

metodo.metaDescription: How a NormaAI answer is made: a corpus of EU acts downloaded from EUR-Lex with a stated date, hybrid retrieval, literal verification of citations, abstention when the text is not enough. Every claim points to the public code file that implements it.
metodo.title: How an answer is made, and when it does not come.
metodo.intro: We publish the method and the code. This page describes the pipeline as it is today, without counters and without promises: every section points to the files of the public repository that implement it, so you can verify instead of believe.

corpus.title: The corpus: official texts, with a date
corpus.p1: The answer corpus contains 18 EU acts, in Italian and English, downloaded from CELLAR, the repository of the Publications Office of the European Union behind EUR-Lex. When one exists, the latest consolidated text is indexed, that is the act with the later amendments already inserted. Today the corpus contains no Italian national law. The texts are split by article; every chunk keeps the act (CELEX), the article, the section title, the language and the date.
corpus.p2: The 18 acts in the acquisition list:

1.name: CSRD
1.acts: Dir. (EU) 2022/2464, the Accounting Directive 2013/34/EU, ESRS (Delegated Reg. (EU) 2023/2772), the stop-the-clock directive (Dir. (EU) 2025/794) and Omnibus I (Dir. (EU) 2026/470)

2.name: CSDDD
2.acts: Dir. (EU) 2024/1760, with the two amending directives already counted above

3.name: AI Act
3.acts: Reg. (EU) 2024/1689 and Reg. (EU) 2026/1744 (Digital Omnibus on AI)

4.name: DORA
4.acts: Reg. (EU) 2022/2554, Delegated Regs (EU) 2024/1773 and 2024/1774, Implementing Reg. (EU) 2024/2956

corpus.p3: The corpus does not update by itself. The periodic acquisition cycle exists in the code but is off by default: the corpus is re-indexed through explicit operations, and the reference date (corpus_as_of) is set at deploy time, returned in the metadata of every API answer and printed in the footer of the reports. Texts superseded by later acts are excluded from the search by default.

pipeline.title: The pipeline, step by step
pipeline.lead: Every question goes through these steps in order. The numbers quoted are the thresholds set in the code, not measured results.

1.title: Hybrid retrieval
1.body: The question is searched in two ways at once: by meaning, with dense vectors of the multilingual model paraphrase-multilingual-mpnet-base-v2 (768 dimensions, chosen because the corpus is in Italian and English and most questions come in Italian), and by exact terms, with BM25-style sparse vectors that capture "Article 29" or a CELEX number. The two rankings are merged with Reciprocal Rank Fusion, with no weights to tune. Filters exclude superseded texts and limit the search to the shared corpus plus the organisation’s documents. A reranking model exists in the code and is off by default.

2.title: Drafting from the retrieved text
2.body: The model receives the question, the company profile if entered and the retrieved passages, with the instruction to cite act and article and not to invent acts or articles that do not exist. The user’s text never enters the system prompt. The model is that of the external provider chosen in the configuration: today, by default, Google Gemini.

3.title: Source-grounding check
3.body: Every citation in the answer is compared with the retrieved passages: the regulation, the CELEX numbers in the text, the article number and the quoted sentence must exist in the evidence. An unsupported citation does not block the answer, but marks it as "expert review needed" and caps its reliability level.

4.title: Literal verification of citations
4.body: It is a deterministic check that does not depend on a model: the passage the answer quotes is looked up in the official text retrieved. Since November 2026 a quote counts as verified only when it is literal: numbers, short words and negations must coincide exactly; only punctuation, accents, line-break hyphenation and a one-letter slip inside a long word are tolerated. Text from documents uploaded by an organisation never counts as official text. If an answer has citations and none is verified, it is served with a warning and the expert-review flag; the configuration can replace it with an abstention instead.

5.title: Multiple sampling, off by default
5.body: The system can generate several independent answers (3 in the initial configuration) and group them by behaviour, to derive a computed confidence score instead of one declared by the model: above 0.85 the answer passes; below 0.50, or if not even two samples agree, the system abstains and says so. At the same stage, if the best retrieved evidence is weak (dense similarity below 0.25), the answer is flagged for review. This layer multiplies the model calls and is off by default: while it stays off, the reliability level starts from the model’s own estimate and is capped by the two checks above.

6.title: Chain-of-Verification, on request
6.body: A five-stage verification exists (claim extraction, verification questions, answers to those questions, revision, validation of the CELEX and URN references), but it is off by default and is enabled per request, only for answers with confidence below 0.85. It is not applied to every answer.

items.1: The act and the article cited, the passage quoted and the link to the official text.
items.2: For every citation, its status: "Verified" when the passage was found word for word in the official text, "Unverified" when it was not.
items.3: A reliability level expressed in words, not a percentage.
items.4: The "expert review needed" flag when the system abstains, when a citation is unsupported or when no citation is verified.
items.5: The notice that the answers are generated by an artificial intelligence system (Reg. (EU) 2024/1689, Art. 50): in the application footer, on the Ask page and in the reports.

data.title: Data and separation between organisations
data.p1: The site is on Vercel; the API, the database and the search index are designed to run on a Hetzner server in Germany. The question, with the retrieved passages, is sent to the configured language-model provider. Each organisation sees only its own data: Row Level Security in PostgreSQL on the tables holding the organisations’ data, with a non-superuser role; per-organisation cache keys; a per-organisation filter in the search engine. The administrator can export and erase the organisation’s data from the application.
data.p2: The details, and what is still missing (SSO, certifications, penetration test), are on the <securityPage>Security</securityPage> page.

ci.title: How we check the code
ci.p1: On every push: lint and format (ruff), type-check (mypy, blocking on the security modules), backend tests on real PostgreSQL, Qdrant and Redis, including a test with two organisations that fails the build if one sees the other’s data; type-check, tests and build of the frontend; CodeQL, Gitleaks, Bandit, Trivy and an SBOM.
ci.p2: Test counts change with every commit: that is why we do not print them here. They can be read in the latest CI run on the repository.

choices.title: Choices you can read in the code
choices.lead: The decisions that matter are annotated next to the code that implements them, even when they correct a mistake of ours.

1.title: Multilingual embedding model
1.body: The English-only embedding model degraded search over Italian legal text. Switching to the multilingual model required re-indexing the whole corpus, because the vectors live in a space specific to the model.

2.title: Stated corpus date
2.body: The corpus is frozen between one re-indexing and the next, and the "superseded" status of an act is set only at that stage. Until repeal detection is automatic, the honest mitigation is to state the corpus date in every answer and in every report.

3.title: Periodic update switched off
3.body: A periodic acquisition cycle existed on paper but did not really run. It is now explicitly off by default, until a dedicated process manages it: better an explicit, dated re-indexing than an untrue "updated every night".

4.title: Optional Chain-of-Verification
4.body: The five-stage verification adds further model calls for every answer. It is available on request, not promised on everything. The same goes for multiple sampling, off by default: the always-on checks are source grounding and the literal verification of citations.

5.title: Cyber Resilience Act on the list
5.body: The CRA was added to the acquisition list together with the implementing regulation on product categories, noting the application dates next to the CELEX numbers (reporting obligations from 11 September 2026, full application from 11 December 2027).
